statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down Jdp2 in Mir137 knockout microglia significantly alleviated both their impaired phagocytosis and their pro-inflammatory response.
statements.evidence: knockdown of Jdp2 significantly suppresses the impaired phagocytosis and pro-inflammatory response in Mir137 knockout microglia
statements.note: The abstract reports that Jdp2 knockdown significantly suppresses the impaired phagocytosis and pro-inflammatory response of Mir137 knockout microglia.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: miR-137 prevents Pu.1 from binding chromatin by physically interacting with the Pu.1 protein in the microglial nucleus.
statements.evidence: we propose that miR-137 modulates Pu.1-mediated gene expression by suppressing Pu.1 binding to chromatin
statements.note: The abstract says miR-137 suppresses Pu.1 binding to chromatin but does not say how, and reports no physical interaction between miR-137 and the Pu.1 protein.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting Mir137 in microglia increased chromatin accessibility at regions containing binding motifs for the master transcription factor Pu.1.
statements.evidence: microglial Mir137 deletion increases chromatin accessibility, which contains binding motifs for the microglial master transcription factor Pu.1
statements.note: The abstract states that microglial Mir137 deletion increases chromatin accessibility at regions with Pu.1 binding motifs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within microglia, miR-137 is enriched in the nucleus, where it helps maintain the cells' global transcriptomic state, phagocytosis and inflammatory response.
statements.evidence: we uncover the enrichment of miR-137, a neuropsychiatric-disorder-associated miRNA, in the microglial nucleus, and reveal its unexpected nuclear functions in maintaining the microglial global transcriptomic state, phagocytosis, and inflammatory response
statements.note: The abstract reports nuclear enrichment of miR-137 in microglia and nuclear functions in maintaining their transcriptomic state, phagocytosis and inflammatory response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By indirectly lowering several neuro- and insulin-like peptides and their secretion machinery, miR-71 decreased mitochondrial stress signalling from muscle to glial cells.
statements.evidence: Indirectly, miR-71 also reduces the levels of multiple neuro- and insulin-like peptides and their secretion machinery, resulting in decreased cell-non-autonomous signaling of mitochondrial stress from muscle to glia cells
statements.note: The abstract reports that miR-71 indirectly reduces these peptides and their secretion machinery, which decreases mitochondrial stress signalling from muscle to glia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When mtDNA is damaged in C. elegans, a protective miRNA response disrupts mitochondrial stress signalling and thereby extends tissue health and function.
statements.evidence: Here we uncover a protective micro(mi)RNA response to mtDNA damage in Caenorhabditis elegans that prolongs tissue health and function by interfering with mitochondrial stress signaling
statements.note: The abstract describes a protective miRNA response to mtDNA damage in C. elegans that prolongs tissue health and function by interfering with mitochondrial stress signalling.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Targeted small RNAs alleviate metabolic disorders in mammals by limiting overactive mitochondrial stress responses.
statements.evidence: These findings open the possibility that metabolic disorders could be ameliorated by limiting the overactivation of mitochondrial stress responses through targeted small RNAs
statements.note: The abstract raises this only as a possibility suggested by the worm data and reports no work on metabolic disorders or mammals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: miR-71 restores sarcomere structure and locomotion by directly curbing excessive activation of DVE-1, a key regulator of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response.
statements.evidence: it restores sarcomere structure and animal locomotion by directly suppressing the inordinate activation of DVE-1, a key regulator of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response
statements.note: The abstract states that miR-71 restores sarcomere structure and locomotion by directly suppressing the inordinate activation of the UPRmt regulator DVE-1.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: miR-305 controls Dmp53 levels in the fat body by directly pairing with the 3' untranslated region of Dmp53 mRNA.
statements.evidence: dMyc-dependent expression of miR-305 in the fat body modulates Dmp53 levels depending on nutrient availability
statements.note: The abstract says miR-305 modulates Dmp53 levels but gives no mechanism, so direct binding to the Dmp53 3' UTR is neither stated nor ruled out.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Fat-body depletion of dMyc prolonged survival under nutrient deprivation, and expressing miR-305 or a dominant negative form of Dmp53 reversed this effect.
statements.evidence: dMyc depletion in the fat body resulted in extended survival to nutrient deprivation which was reverted by expression of either miR-305 or a dominant negative version of Dmp53
statements.note: The abstract reports extended survival to nutrient deprivation after fat-body dMyc depletion, reverted by miR-305 or dominant negative Dmp53 expression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analysis of ChIP-Seq data showed that close to 56% of Drosophila miRNA genes are bound by dMyc, with canonical or non-canonical E-boxes in the peaks.
statements.evidence: nearly 56% of Drosophila miRNA genes show dMyc binding, exhibiting either the canonical or non-canonical E-box sequences within the peak region
statements.note: The abstract reports dMyc binding at nearly 56% of Drosophila miRNA genes from ChIP-Seq data, with canonical or non-canonical E-boxes in the peaks.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Lowering dMyc levels led to a widespread downregulation of miRNA gene expression.
statements.evidence: reduction of dMyc levels resulted in widespread downregulation of miRNAs gene expression
statements.note: The abstract states that reducing dMyc levels resulted in widespread downregulation of miRNA gene expression.
